questions.q: I enjoy ___ to music in the evening.
questions.why: 'Enjoy' is always followed by a gerund (-ing).

questions.q: You should avoid ___ so much sugar.
questions.why: 'Avoid' takes a gerund, never an infinitive.

questions.q: Have you finished ___ your homework?
questions.why: 'Finish' is followed by a gerund.

questions.q: They want ___ a new house next year.
questions.why: 'Want' is followed by the infinitive with 'to'.

questions.q: We decided ___ early in the morning.
questions.why: 'Decide' takes the infinitive with 'to'.

questions.q: She hopes ___ the exam this time.
questions.why: 'Hope' is followed by the infinitive.

questions.q: He stopped ___ because his legs hurt.
questions.why: 'Stop + gerund' means to quit the activity itself.

questions.q: On the way home he stopped ___ some bread.
questions.why: 'Stop + infinitive' shows the purpose for stopping.

questions.q: Please remember ___ the door when you leave.
questions.why: 'Remember + infinitive' means not to forget a future task.

questions.q: I remember ___ him at the party last year.
questions.why: 'Remember + gerund' refers to a past memory.

questions.q: Don't forget ___ me when you arrive.
questions.why: 'Forget + infinitive' is about a future duty.

questions.q: I will never forget ___ the ocean for the first time.
questions.why: 'Forget + gerund' refers to a memorable past experience.

questions.q: My computer froze, so I tried ___ it.
questions.why: 'Try + gerund' means to experiment with a solution.

questions.q: The shelf is high, so she tried ___ the box but couldn't reach.
questions.why: 'Try + infinitive' means to attempt something difficult.

questions.q: He is good ___ solving puzzles.
questions.why: After a preposition like 'at', use a gerund.

questions.q: They are interested in ___ Spanish.
questions.why: A verb after a preposition must be a gerund.

questions.q: Thank you for ___ me.
questions.why: After the preposition 'for', use the -ing form.

questions.q: She apologised for ___ late.
questions.why: Prepositions are always followed by a gerund.

questions.q: It is important ___ on time.
questions.why: After 'it is + adjective', use the infinitive with 'to'.

questions.q: This problem is hard ___ .
questions.why: An adjective like 'hard' is followed by the infinitive.

questions.q: I am happy ___ you again.
questions.why: Adjectives describing feelings take the infinitive.

questions.q: He used a knife ___ the rope.
questions.why: Use 'to + verb' to express purpose with an action.

questions.q: This tool is used ___ wood.
questions.why: Use 'for + gerund' to describe a thing's general function.

questions.q: She suggested ___ a taxi.
questions.why: 'Suggest' is followed by a gerund, not an infinitive.

questions.q: We can't afford ___ a new car.
questions.why: 'Afford' takes the infinitive with 'to'.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'I enjoy ___ (cook) for my family.'
questions.why: 'Enjoy' is always followed by the gerund.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'They decided ___ (move) abroad.'
questions.why: 'Decide' is followed by the infinitive with 'to'.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'She is afraid of ___ (fly).'
questions.why: After the preposition 'of', use the gerund.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'It was nice ___ (meet) you.'
questions.why: Adjectives like 'nice' are followed by the infinitive.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'He went to the shop ___ (buy) milk.'
questions.why: Use 'to + verb' to express the purpose of an action.

questions.q: He suggested ___ early to avoid traffic.
questions.why: 'Suggest' is followed by a gerund.

questions.q: I can't afford ___ a new car this year.
questions.why: 'Afford' is followed by the to-infinitive.

questions.q: She stopped ___ when the teacher came in.
questions.why: 'Stop + -ing' = quit the activity; 'stop to talk' = pause in order to talk.

questions.q: Remember ___ the door when you leave.
questions.why: 'Remember to do' = don't forget a duty; 'remember doing' = recall a memory.

questions.q: It's no use ___ about it now.
questions.why: 'It's no use' + gerund is a fixed pattern.
